source_snapshot.scope: Scoped current-main path and source census. Candidate PR branches are recorded separately and are not treated as merged or qualified.
source_snapshot.duplicate_workspace_note: The repository contains top-level and mycelix-workspace copies of several projects. Inspected support-ticket and civic files in those copies had identical blob SHAs; this census does not infer which copy is the future canonical build root.

candidates.scope_limit: Generic Mycelix support tickets; not a Johannesburg Water or City CRM record.
candidates.finding: SupportTicket stores generic operational fields but no separate stable logical municipal issue ID. The inspected integrity update callback revalidates ticket shape; it does not compare original content to establish immutable-field rules or Civic-specific transition constraints. No municipal reference or verified repair state is present.

candidates.semantic_concern: Mycelix-internal ticket creation, update and close operations
candidates.finding: create_ticket creates requester/status/category links. update_ticket accepts a whole replacement SupportTicket and updates the entry; close_ticket updates status to Closed. The inspected update/close paths do not visibly reindex status/category links. The separate integrity RegisterUpdate author-match check is not proof of immutable fields, transition algebra, current status index, or civic authority.

candidates.scope_limit: General support domain vocabulary; not a municipal service taxonomy or SLA registry.
candidates.finding: TicketStatus and TicketPriority exist, but do not define utility-specific response clocks, field dispatch states or source-system currentness.

candidates.semantic_concern: Shared justice/media evidence and custody concepts
candidates.scope_limit: General evidence types; not a Johannesburg municipal repair-verification implementation.
candidates.finding: Evidence and custody structures exist, but an attested evidence record is not by itself proof that a repair occurred or that service was restored.

candidates.scope_limit: Formal dispute procedure, not routine municipal service request intake or work-order tracking.
candidates.finding: Case phases/statuses represent disputes, mediation/arbitration and enforcement; repurposing these would conflate service operations and adjudication.

candidates.semantic_concern: Cross-domain dispatch and event/query transport inside Commons
candidates.scope_limit: Internal Mycelix cluster bridge; no Johannesburg provider/API adapter established.
candidates.finding: The bridge routes among Commons domains and broadcasts internal events; this does not establish external City API access, acceptance semantics, authentication, currentness or idempotent provider submission.

candidates.scope_limit: Displays Mycelix community water-system capacity/fill/steward data; not municipal resident intake.
candidates.finding: A display page is not proof of an operational case intake, utility fault-routing or repair-closure workflow.

candidates.semantic_concern: Water harvesting, storage and stewardship domain
candidates.scope_limit: Resource/capture records, not municipal fault/request lifecycle.
candidates.finding: Models harvesting systems, tanks and capture/recharge records; it is not a utility pipe-break repair queue.

candidates.scope_limit: Product/BOM/routing work orders; not municipal service requests.
candidates.finding: Has manufacturing-specific work order/status transition types. Its presence does not justify reusing it as a municipal ticket owner.

candidates.semantic_concern: Stable municipal service-issue identity and end-to-end operational state
candidates.scope_limit: No suitable authoritative municipal service-issue runtime identified in the scoped current-main census.
candidates.finding: Do not infer global absence from scoped search; current main did not expose an approved municipal runtime or adapter. Existing generic ActionHash/revision identity is not a municipal logical identity contract.

candidates.semantic_concern: Authorised City/utility source-system adapter and currentness mapping
candidates.scope_limit: No provider contract, API access grant or City integration established.
candidates.finding: City/utility reference numbers must remain external references; successful local persistence or submission must not be interpreted as municipal acceptance or current status.

candidates.semantic_concern: Versioned municipal service-level definitions and SLA clocks
candidates.scope_limit: No current approved Joburg-specific SLA registry found in the inspected current-main implementation.
candidates.finding: The City document index lists 2026/27 planning documents and a 2025/26 service-standards charter. The charter is a reference baseline only until the current adopted target, clock semantics and effective dates are verified.

candidates.semantic_concern: Municipal completion-claim, evidence and independent verification adapter
candidates.scope_limit: No municipal repair-closure verification implementation identified in the inspected current-main surfaces.
candidates.finding: Ticket status, an official-looking receipt, a contractor claim and a verified physical outcome are distinct artifacts.

candidates.semantic_concern: Administrative procedure for rights-affecting government decisions
candidates.scope_limit: No exact ADMIN-001/002/003 path identified by the scoped current-main census; broader absence is not asserted.
candidates.finding: Routine service resolution must not become an AI-made benefits, entitlement, billing-dispute, disconnection or licensing decision.

candidates.semantic_concern: External source submission, retry and offline/idempotency contract
candidates.scope_limit: No City provider adapter or external idempotency contract identified.
candidates.finding: A retry after a timeout must not silently create duplicate City requests; do not promise at-most-once or exactly-once behavior without provider semantics and tests.

owner_matrix.decision: Block implementation. Current-main generic ticket ActionHash/revision identity does not establish the stable municipal issue identity; SUP-CIV-001A is an open branch-only proposal.
Useful internal create/update history exists, but there is no verified linkage to a City/utility-originated intake record or source currentness.
The internal status enum is only local Mycelix state; external currentness remains unimplemented and must be sourced from an authorised provider.
An optional internal assignee exists; a municipal team/vehicle/spares/dispatch contract was not identified. Keep Symthaea output advisory.
Existing water UI is a resource dashboard, not evidence of resident fault intake or accessible multi-channel municipal reporting.
Reuse evidence concepts only after the adapter defines protected storage/reference policy; evidence creation does not imply verification.
Do not implement or automate consequential resident decisions until the legitimate procedure/authority owner is identified and bound.
Preserve the City/utility reference as a typed external source reference; do not mint it locally or treat a mirror as current.
Johannesburg Water's public incident email/call-centre and system-wide bulletin are distinct resident-facing channels; no machine API or per-case status/repair proof is established.

The public Daily Water Notices turnaround list uses operational categories/times that are not proven equivalent to budget-book percentage targets or the listed prior-year charter; no adopted crosswalk/clock registry is pinned.

The official /daily-water-notices/ and /emergencies/ routes render the same Daily water Notices heading with different sewer/water-outage windows, logging channels and contact numbers. No effective-date or page-precedence rule is present in the observed text; preserve both source variants and block canonical target/contact claims.

The dedicated Contact Us body provides purpose-labelled incident logging and interruption-notification details, while generic footers/other routes diverge. Preserve the exact page/section/role; do not infer cross-page precedence or automation authority.

The Services page mixes notice lead times, response targets, attempted restoration, working-day repair/install windows and test-result targets. Preserve verb/clock semantics and unknown effective date; do not treat the 12-hour emergency response target as a restoration deadline.
Keep commitment, completion claim, evidence bundle, predicate verification and downstream outcome as distinct artifacts.
No SLA math until official target source/version, clock start/stop, pauses/exclusions, denominator and reopen treatment are explicit.
No live provider retry path without a qualified idempotency key, timeout reconciliation, duplicate-submission behavior and stale/offline rules.
Water capture/stewardship models are not municipal repair operations.
Manufacturing work orders must not be promoted into a public-works owner based on structural similarity.
Keep routine service tickets distinct from legal or quasi-judicial cases.
Internal cross-domain event/query routing is not proof of an authorised external municipal integration.
Symthaea may propose grouping, urgency and routing only; it must not create municipal authority or trigger state-changing actions.
Whole-ticket replacement plus field-shape checks does not prove immutable-field restrictions. No Civic writes until an exact-head adversarial contract qualifies.
Status/category link maintenance is not visibly performed by ordinary update/close paths; status-index currentness remains unqualified.
Support update path does not itself establish a Civic-specific typed transition algebra; require explicit allowed transitions and rejection tests.
Support autonomy/approved/executed/success fields are Support-domain state and must not confer civic or municipal action authority.

source_anchors.purpose: Official source index for the 2026/27 IDP/SDBIP and service-level standards documents; listing is not evidence of an integration grant.
Statutory review anchor; legal review triggers are not legal conclusions.
Existing City contact/service channel reference; does not expose or authorize a machine interface.
Official resident-facing fault/query instructions; follow-up should use an existing reference to prevent duplicate official queries. Website availability does not imply API authority.
Official description of the unit responsible for maintaining the Service Level Standards Charter and quarterly monitoring; this mandate is not itself a current adopted target.
Official channel FAQ describing reference-number allocation and forwarding to service providers; not a machine interface contract.

Official final budget PDF opened through the document viewer; extracted text exposes section 2.3.4 and Joburg Water service standards on printed page 125. The page screenshot timed out, and this does not establish an adopted institutional charter or live case status.
The official City index links a 2026/27 SDBIP PDF. Opening the linked PDF timed out in this pass; its metrics have not been reconciled against the budget-book table.

Official Johannesburg Water website lists water-incident fault email/contact channels and a daily water-supply system status update; these are public channel/bulletin references, not an API grant, per-case readback, or repair proof.

Linked as Customer Fault Logging by the official Johannesburg Water website; opens a third-party Forcelink JavaScript login page. This is a resident-facing portal route, not an API contract or authorization for automated access.

Official Johannesburg Water daily notices page publishes operational turnaround statements and contact details; those values are kept separate from budget-book percentage targets and from individual-case completion evidence.

Official route titled Emergencies was crawled on 2026-10-13 but renders a Daily water Notices heading and a different turnaround/contact block from /daily-water-notices/. No effective-date, version or cross-page precedence rule is given; scope relationship is unresolved.

Official Contact Us body explicitly labels a contact centre number and email for logging calls/queries, and a separate email for interruption notifications. Its generic footer has different formatting/details; treat purpose-labelled body fields separately and do not infer global precedence over other official routes.

Official Services page labels a table CUSTOMER SERVICE STANDARDS TARGET. It mixes advance notification lead times, response targets, repair/replace windows in working days, attempts to restore supplies, and customer-response/sample-result targets. No effective date/version was visible in the extracted page text; these are not automatically the City's adopted institutional SLA or equivalent to Daily Water Notices turnaround rows.

decision.internal_candidate: Commons Support is a read-only operational-owner candidate until stable identity, immutable-field rules, typed transitions, status/category index currentness and the autonomy boundary are qualified; not a canonical municipal service issue owner.
decision.authoritative_source: The City or utility remains the external authority for its own reference number and current operational status, once the relevant source system and authorised interface are identified.
required_preconditions: Resolve the owner/adaptor census with reviewers and confirm path/build-root authority.
Qualify stable internal issue identity; do not assume the unmerged SUP-CIV-001A branch is active.
Identify the actual City/utility system owner, provider contract, lawful access route and source-currentness semantics.
Bind current approved service-standard source and exact clock/start/stop/reopen rules.
Define data minimisation, protected storage, retention, access/deletion, legal and privacy review.
Qualify idempotent retry/offline behaviour and preserve each original report and its own SLA clock.
Keep completion claim, submitted evidence, independent predicate verification and downstream outcome distinct.
Run synthetic/replay and then shadow evaluation before any restricted operational trial.

invariants: City/utility reference number != Mycelix stable service issue ID.
Local mirror != authoritative current City/utility status.
Successful local submission != municipal acceptance.
Municipal acceptance != physical repair or service restoration.
Ticket closed != verified repair.
Completion claim != completion evidence != independent verification != outcome improvement.
Deduplication must never erase reports, identities, timestamps or individual service clocks.
Symthaea recommendation != approval, execution capability, civic authority or legal decision.
A signed receipt proves a bounded attestation/provenance statement, not physical truth by itself.
An open branch or queued check != merged code, qualified contract or passed evidence.
An external reference is namespaced by issuer and channel; its bare string is not a global identity.
Same-reference follow-up appends to the existing external case and must not cause a duplicate official intake.
The City's resident-facing website is not evidence of API authorization.
A resident-reported status is not verified external currentness.
A previous-year service-level charter is not an adopted current-year target.
Keep raw resident references and protected details out of public DHTs and public receipts.
A 2026/27 budget-book service target and a 2025/26 charter target are versioned separately.
The 2026/27 planned-interruption measure is not equivalent to the prior 12-hour general interruption measure.
An indexed target is not a live status observation or proof that a specific issue met the target.
Do not calculate compliance while target scope, source review or required clock semantics are unresolved.

documented_claims.published_fact: The website lists fault@jwater.co.za for logging water-related incidents only.
The website links to a Daily water supply system status update.
The website lists call-centre numbers +27 (0) 10 061 4470 and +27 (0) 86 056 2874.
The official homepage Customer Fault Logging link opens https://customer.forcelink.net/joburg_water/login, a third-party Forcelink JavaScript portal/login.
The Daily Water Notices page lists sewer 48 hours, water outage 24 hours, leaking meter 72 hours, burst meter 24 hours, water leak 48 hours and major burst pipe 48 hours.

The official /emergencies/ route currently renders the same Daily water Notices heading but lists sewer 24 hours and water outage 12 hours, plus a different logging email and contact-centre number, compared with /daily-water-notices/.

Contact Us body says To log calls/queries: +27 (0)10 061 4470 and fault@jwater.co.za; for interruption notifications it lists sms@jwater.co.za. The footer separately displays a differently formatted contact-centre number.

external_utility_channel_contract.reference_namespace_collision_policy: A different issuer or channel defines a distinct namespace; equal opaque reference strings must not be auto-merged.
external_utility_channel_contract.system_status_update_policy: Capture as a source-tagged, time-stamped utility-wide observation only; it cannot set an individual issue to resolved without explicit case linkage and a separate verification predicate.
external_utility_channel_contract.utility_fault_email_scope: Water-related incidents only, as stated by the published site
external_utility_channel_contract.portal_authentication_boundary: Official Johannesburg Water site links to a third-party Forcelink login route. The page requires JavaScript; no provider API contract, automated access permission, per-case readback contract or completion proof was identified.
external_utility_channel_contract.turnaround_semantics_policy: Published customer-facing turnaround statements remain a separate source class from budget-book percentage performance targets and the separately listed institutional charter. Similar labels or nominal hours do not prove identical scope, denominator, clock, remedy or adopted SLA. No automatic crosswalk or SLA compliance calculation is authorized.
external_utility_channel_contract.contact_numbers_use_policy: The Daily Water Notices page shows different primary contact-centre numbers in its Logging calls section and footer. Preserve the source section; do not silently canonicalize this conflict without independent confirmation.

published_page_conflicts.route_scope_relationship: Unresolved; route path and heading alone do not establish whether this is an emergency-specific policy, stale duplicated content, or another variant.
forbidden_inferences: Do not choose one page as authoritative solely because the route name contains emergencies.
Do not treat crawler observation date as target effective date.
Do not claim any phone/email value is verified current solely from the page block.
Do not infer the 12-hour water outage figure is equivalent to the budget-book planned-interruption target.

customer_contact_instructions.interpretation: The explicit body labels are evidence for their named purposes. The body/footer differ in contact-number format/value; no source rule establishes a global override of other official routes. Preserve page, section, role and observation time.

customer_service_standards.semantics_policy: Do not collapse action verbs: Notify != Respond != Restore != RepairOrReplace != Install != ProvideTestResult. WorkingDays != calendar days; 'endeavour/attempt' is not an unconditional completion guarantee. Advance notice is not a post-report repair clock. No production breach/status calculation until version/effective period, clock start/end, exclusions and adopted authority are qualified.
